hooks.text: The solar system's fastest winds howl across freezing Neptune.
Could the coldest planet harbor the solar system's fastest winds?
Voyager 2 found the solar system's fastest winds on Neptune.

title: The Solar System's Fastest Winds Blew on Neptune
description: When Voyager 2 swept past Neptune in 1989, it discovered supersonic winds and active ice volcanoes at the outer edge of our solar system.

beats.text: The solar system's fastest winds howl across freezing Neptune.
beats.visual: Voyager 2 full disk photo of Neptune showing blue cloud bands, 1989

beats.text: Atmospheric methane gives the ice giant its vivid blue color.
beats.visual: Close-up color image of Neptune atmosphere taken by Voyager 2, 1989

beats.text: The probe swooped just 3,000 miles over its north pole.
beats.visual: Diagram of Voyager 2 trajectory skimming above Neptune north pole, 1989

beats.text: It recorded atmospheric winds topping 1,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Voyager 2 high resolution detail of white cloud streaks on Neptune, 1989
queries: Neptune high speed winds voyager detail

beats.text: An Earth-sized storm named the Great Dark Spot raged below.
beats.visual: Voyager 2 photo of Neptune Great Dark Spot storm detail, 1989

beats.text: Voyager 2 also confirmed four rings and six new moons.
beats.visual: Long exposure photo of Neptune faint ring system captured by Voyager 2, 1989

beats.text: On Triton, active ice volcanoes erupted at minus 391 degrees Fahrenheit.
beats.visual: Voyager 2 photograph of moon Triton showing geyser deposits and icy terrain, 1989
queries: Triton surface ice volcanoes NASA voyager

beats.text: To celebrate the final flyby, rock legend Chuck Berry played live at JPL.
beats.visual: Photograph of Chuck Berry performing live at NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, 1989

beats.text: It remains the only spacecraft that ever visited distant Neptune.
beats.visual: Full view photo of Voyager 2 spacecraft artwork drifting into deep space, 1989

hook_text: FASTEST WINDS IN THE SOLAR SYSTEM
better_than_last: Applies the proven myth_vs_fact structure to contrast expectations of quiet frozen skies with supersonic 1,000 mph winds, concluding with the unexpected Chuck Berry JPL celebration before looping back into the opening image.
